paper.title: Online Influence Maximization under Linear Threshold Model

settings.name_in_paper: OIM under LT model with node-level feedback (LT-LinUCB, anytime confidence parameter)
unmapped: Online influence maximization: action is a seed set of at most K nodes (K_seed) in a known directed graph with n nodes and m edges; reward is the influence spread (nonlinear, monotone, Lipschitz in edge weights) under the linear threshold model with unknown edge weights and uniform random node thresholds
Node-level feedback: learner observes the sequence of activated node sets S_{t,0}, S_{t,1}, ... (aggregated group effects of in-neighbors, not individual edges)
Edge weights satisfy sum of incoming weights <= 1 for every node
Learner knows the graph structure G
Regret is alpha*beta-scaled regret against an (alpha,beta)-approximation offline oracle
settings.definition_quote: The objective of the OIM is to minimize the cumulative $\eta$-scaled regret over total $T$ rounds: R(T) = E[\eta T Opt_w - \sum_t r(S_t,w)] ... we consider a more realistic node-level feedback: the learner can only observe the influence diffusion process on node sets as $S_{t,0},\ldots,S_{t,\tau},\ldots$ in round $t$.

settings.name_in_paper: OIM under LT model with node-level feedback (known horizon and minimum gap)
unmapped: Online influence maximization: seed set of at most K nodes in a known directed graph with n nodes and m edges; influence spread reward under LT (OIM-ETC also applies to IC) with unknown edge weights
Node-level feedback; OIM-ETC only uses first-step activations
Learner knows the graph structure G
Regret is alpha*beta-scaled regret; gaps defined relative to alpha*Opt_w over bad seed sets
settings.definition_quote: (Gaps of bad seed sets) For a bad seed set $S \in \mathcal{S}_B$, its gap is defined as $\Delta_S := \alpha \cdot \opt_w - r(S, w)$.

symbols.gamma_G: graph constant max_S sqrt(sum_u N_{S,u}^2) <= (n-K) sqrt(n)

conditions: sum of incoming edge weights at each node <= 1

source.label: main theorem
source.quote: Suppose the $\ltlinucb$ runs with an $(\alpha,\beta)$-approximation $\pairoracle$ and parameter $\rho_{t,v} = \rho_t = \sqrt{n \log(1+tn)+2\log\frac{1}{\delta}} + \sqrt{n}$ for any node $v \in V$. Then the $\alpha \beta$-scaled regret satisfies R(T) \le 2\rho_T \gamma(G) D \sqrt{mnT \log(1+T) / \log(1+n)} + n\delta \cdot T(n-k).

results.notes: Regret is alpha*beta-scaled regret in expectation over thresholds and oracle randomness. The paper writes (n-k) with lower-case k, which presumably means the seed size K. Feedback is mapped to partial_monitoring because node-level feedback has no exact vocabulary term. The PairOracle (WCIM) may not be efficient for general graphs.

conditions: sum of incoming edge weights at each node <= 1

source.label: main theorem
source.quote: When $\delta = 1/ (n\sqrt{T})$, $R(T) \le C \cdot \gamma(G) \  D n\sqrt{mT} \log(T)$ for some universal constant $C$.

results.notes: Universal constant C. For general graphs this is O(n^{7/2} m^{1/2} sqrt(T) ln T) per the appendix.

conditions: Delta_min, Delta_max are gaps of bad seed sets relative to alpha*Opt_w
tuning: k = max{1, 2 m^2 n^2/Delta_min^2 * ln(T Delta_min^2/(m n^3))}

source.label: thm:etc
source.quote: When $k = \max\set{1, \frac{2m^2 n^2}{\Delta_{\min}^2}\ln\bracket{\frac{T \Delta_{\min}^2}{m n^3}}  }$, the $\alpha\beta$-scaled regret bound of our $\oimetc$ algorithm over $T$ rounds satisfies R(T) \leq \min\{T\Delta_{\max}, n\Delta_{\max} + \frac{2m^2 n^3\Delta_{\max}}{\Delta_{\min}^2}(1 + \max\{0,\ln(\frac{T\Delta_{\min}^2}{mn^3})\})\} = O(\frac{m^2 n^3\Delta_{\max}}{\Delta_{\min}^2} \ln(T)).

results.notes: Delta_min/Delta_max here are gaps of bad seed sets w.r.t. alpha*Opt_w (Definition 2), not arm gaps. OIM-ETC applies to both LT and IC models; only one offline oracle call.

source.label: thm:etc
source.quote: When $k = 3.9 (m^2T/n)^{2/3}$, the $\alpha\beta$-scaled regret bound of $\oimetc$ algorithm over $T$ rounds satisfies R(T) \le 3.9(mn)^{4/3} T^{2/3} + 1 =O\bracket{(mn)^{4/3} T^{2/3}}.

results.notes: Applies to both LT and IC models. The proof uses k = 3.9 m^{4/3} n^{-2/3} T^{2/3}, which matches the stated k.
